notes: v10.4 BUILD REFRESH (2026-09-03, b2899 - the trailing-word tune, notarized): The last word of a dictation can no longer vanish. When a dictation ends on a softly spoken word, the clip-tail guard used to take ONE short re-hearing of that tail and, if the re-hearing came back empty, treated the silence as proof and dropped the word ("...continue the work" lost "work"; "...this error or not?" lost "not"). The guard now takes two hearings at different offsets and keeps any word either hearing backs; an all-empty result is treated as no opinion and the word stands. Verified on every reported specimen (7 of 7 lost words present in the replay) and on the full benchmark rig (the empty-output rate on the TED-LIUM set fell from 40% to 2.0% raw / 0.7% edited, with no regression on any other set). Notarized by Apple: macOS opens it without any warning. - see fabledflow.com/changelog.html
